description: Agent Cybersecurity: submit logging records with the logging policy: the policy with the events that must be logged (such as authentication, privilege change or configuration change), the events that must raise an alert, the retention period in days, the hours of silence that count as a gap and its text; each log source with its id, name, the events it logs and its retention in days; each alert with the event it covers, its owner and whether the owner is a person, a role, a channel or no one; and each gap in the log record itself with the source and when the silence began and ended. The signed report gives the policy, the required events with those logged and those no source logs, each source’s retention against the policy, every alert with the events missing an alert, the alerts routed to no one and those routed only to a role or channel, and every recorded gap with its hours and the longest, and counts them, and names logging gaps: an event the policy names that no source logs, a source keeping logs shorter than the policy’s period, an alert routed to no one and a gap in the log longer than the policy allows; then an event that raises no alert where the policy requires one and an alert routed to a role or channel with no named person, with the fix for each and what would change the verdict. No events in the policy, no sources, no retention period or source retention, no alert record where alerts are required, an owner of unknown kind or no record of gaps leaves the logging unverified. Events and alerts match by name without case or punctuation. This reads security logging coverage: wever_observability-log-check reads whether an agent’s log entries name the actor, principal and authorization behind each action, wever_observability-retention-check reads trace and log retention rules against dispute and audit windows, and wever_audit-evidence-check reads a counterparty’s audit report, while the logging check reads which security events are logged, retention as configured, alert routing and gaps in the log itself. Verdict cyber_logging_gap, cyber_logging_partial, cyber_logging_unverified or cyber_logging_covered. POST /api/cyber-logging-check. Reads the security records supplied in the call and returns a signed report with the verdict, the evidence read, the findings with their fixes, and what would change the verdict; the records stay in the report, with no network request, fetch, message, payment, system scan, probe or external write. Agent Cybersecurity reads an organization’s own security records after the fact and checks them against the stated policy and against themselves: standing access, the secrets inventory, the component and patch record, the exported configuration, logging coverage, backup and restore evidence, a vendor’s security evidence and incident readiness. Beside it, the Agent Risk checks such as wever_risk-exposure-check read one planned action’s worst case and limits before it runs, while a cyber check reads security posture from the records; and the security reads elsewhere in the catalog keep their families, each named beside the check it meets. Paid URL: 0.10 USDC per call on Base via x402 exact, with the shared 10 signed-wallet free calls per rolling 30 days. Bind X-Wever-Wallet-Proof to the exact JSON arguments and the tool route. Returns a report with an Ed25519 signed receipt. Contract: /api/agent-cybersecurity-contract. Human page: https://weverlabs.com/agent-cybersecurity/.
